summary: Today’s pulse tracks Five killed in Miami plane crash were in two vehicles on ground, investigators say, Ukrainian TV channel building hit by Russian drone as five killed in Kyiv, and Democrats hit back at Trump after president floats changing name of New Mexico to ‘New America’ - US politics live. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are traffic, issue, and control. In the background, UK air traffic control fix issue that cancelled 300 flights but disruption to continue into evening – business live and Israel to close UK consulate in Jerusalem after sanctions against illegal settlements – UK politics live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Five killed in Miami plane crash were in two vehicles on ground, investigators say
headlines.description: Investigators described the scene as "utter devastation" after a Boeing 767-300 overshot the runway at Miami airport.

headlines.title: Ukrainian TV channel building hit by Russian drone as five killed in Kyiv
headlines.description: President Zelensky describes the daytime drone attack in Ukraine's capital as a "new page in Russian degradation"

headlines.title: Democrats hit back at Trump after president floats changing name of New Mexico to ‘New America’ - US politics live
headlines.description: State senator among politicians hitting back at president’s social media post saying New Mexico should be change to ‘New America’ The district, long purple, has been reliably blue since 2017. Republicans now see it as flippable, and Donald Trump has endorsed Anthony DiLorenzo , a businessman who owns several car dealerships, in the GOP race.

headlinePool.title: Hurricane Lowell brings threat of floods, mudslides and tornadoes to Hawaii
headlinePool.description: Islands of Kauai and Ni’ihau are under hurricane warning, while Oahu is under a tropical storm warning Damaging winds and heavy rains from Hurricane Lowell were pelting Hawaii’s western islands on Tuesday, bringing the threat of floods, mudslides and tornadoes. The islands of Kauai and Ni’ihau are under a hurricane warning, while Oahu, the state’s most populated island with close to 1 million residents, was under a tropical storm warning.

headlinePool.title: Police overlooked tip-off day before far-right agitators blocked Dover roads
headlinePool.description: Details passed to Kent police after people heard in pub boasting about going to Dover to ‘attack Muslims’ Police were told the night before far-right agitators blocked roads into Dover that those involved had converged on a village 18 miles away and planned to use it as a launchpad, it has emerged. People in Preston-next-Wingham told of how hundreds of men had started to arrive in the village of just over 920 residents on Friday afternoon and in effect “took over” the village.

headlinePool.title: Russia says it will give a ‘harsh and painful’ response after Hungary expels 10 diplomats - Europe live
headlinePool.description: Moscow’s foreign minister issues warning to ‘Russophobic lobby in Budapest’ after diplomats expelled for ‘unacceptable’ activities But the tone coming from Moscow is very different, as Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters that Russia was very confident that victory in its war against Ukraine is “very near.” “Yes, we are ​confident, and we ⁠are ​sure that ​victory ​is very near,” ​Peskov ‌said in comments reported by Reuters.

headlinePool.title: Barnaby Webber’s death in Nottingham attack was ‘potentially preventable’, inquiry told
headlinePool.description: More rapid use of blood products may have raised chance of 19-year-old making it to hospital, though chance was low, says counsel The death of a 19-year-old student who was killed in the Nottingham attacks in 2023 was “potentially preventable”, a public inquiry into the incident has heard. Barnaby Webber and Grace O’Malley-Kumar, both 19, and Ian Coates, a 65-year-old caretaker, were fatally stabbed by Valdo Calocane, a paranoid schizophrenic, on 13 June 2023.

headlinePool.title: Sabotage suspect held in Germany after spate of attacks on power grid
headlinePool.description: The suspect had reportedly claimed responsibility for attacks on electricity substations in letters.

headlinePool.title: Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer urges Trump to consider pardon after mistrial
headlinePool.description: Attorney hopes Trump would ‘consider a pardon’ given ‘the type of person she is’ and ‘what she has been through’ Murder trial ends in dramatic deadlock – what comes next The lawyer of Lindsay Clancy , the Massachusetts woman accused of killing her three young children, has said he hopes Donald Trump will pardon his client after her trial recently ended with a deadlocked jury. Clancy’s attorney, Kevin Reddington, made the appeal on a televised interview on the ABC show Good Morning America on Tuesday. The plea comes to Trump after a judge on Friday declared a mistrial after the jury in the Clancy case could not reach a unanimous verdict on whether she was guilty or not guilty. headlinePool.title: British family of man abducted by Saudi Arabia speak out over nine-year ordeal
headlinePool.description: Mira Lozi says quiet diplomacy has failed to free Rami Naimi who was first seized in Dubai in 2017 A British woman has spoken out for the first time about the alleged abduction, torture and coercion of her husband at the hands of Saudi authorities, after nine years of “failed” quiet diplomacy. The businessman Rami Naimi was first abducted in Dubai in 2017 on his return from a trip to Australia with his father. After being tortured, he was released the following year.

headlinePool.title: UK accuses Israeli ‘terrorists’ of ethnic cleansing in West Bank with government backing
headlinePool.description: In strongest condemnation ever by UK government, Ed Miliband announces sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements UK politics live – latest updates Israeli “terrorists” are conducting ethnic cleansing in the West Bank with the tacit backing of the government, the UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband has said, as he announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements. In the strongest condemnation ever issued by the UK government, Miliband said the government would now take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety, saying such acknowledgment was “the least the people who face such suffering deserve. And it should be the prelude to justice.” An import ban on goods from illegal settlements in the occupied territories. A comprehensive sanctions regime against providing services such as construction or financing for Israeli settlements. A ban on the advertising in the UK of illegal settlement properties. Personal sanctions against key individuals accused of promoting settler violence. A new ban for arms licences and other exports that “materially contribute to the occupation”.
